description: We are two Zoomers in IT
summary:
We built a health monitoring tool that helps astronauts on long missions track and understand their own health - even when no doctor can help and there is no link to Earth.

The tool is designed around minimal effort. In microgravity, even tapping a screen is hard, so most data flows in automatically from wearables and ship sensors. Each value is compared with the astronaut’s own pre-flight norm, not an average.

At its heart is an interactive 3D body model with switchable layers. Every part shows a simple green, yellow or red status - the same color system across the whole tool - and a tap explains what is happening and what to do next. Daily tasks, hydration, sleep, mood and exercise are tracked alongside it, and radiation is monitored constantly, with a full-screen alert during solar storms.

Due to the hackathon’s time limit, we built it as a web dashboard. Next, we plan to develop it into a full application for onboard laptops and tablets.
details:
What it does

On missions to Mars, help from Earth is delayed or unavailable. WALL-E & EVE is health software for the crew laptop or tablet. Wearables and ship sensors send data automatically, and a few devices are used by hand (cuff, glucometer, urine strip). Each value is compared with the astronaut’s own pre-flight norm and shown as green, yellow or red on a holographic body, with advice. A daily plan says what to measure and when, and a solar storm triggers an alarm.

Benefits

Little manual input, works offline, catches early changes and turns numbers into clear actions. Critical cases go to the flight surgeon at the first link.

Impact

Deep-space crews must be autonomous. The app helps catch bone loss, dehydration, poor sleep and radiation risks early. Next: an offline AI assistant, a 3D body model, real devices.

Tools

TypeScript, React, Vite, Claude Design and Claude Code. Data is simulated. The final version would be desktop and tablet software on the ship’s network.

Creativity

Each body system has its own look on the hologram, ready to become a 3D model where the astronaut zooms in and picks an organ. The plan adapts: status decides what to measure, and each measurement updates the status.

Factors

Delays and blackouts, space hazards, busy astronauts, safety (the app never replaces the flight surgeon) and no stressful numbers without an action.
